openai.sample_unit: obstetric ultrasound scans across remote expert–reviewed and AI-supported workflows

links.outcome: Sufficient-quality ultrasound scans with versus without in-app tutorial videos
links.effect: Sufficient scans: 85.3% with tutorials versus 43.2% without (OR: 14.1, 95% CI: 6.40–31.12, p < 0.001). App version was confounded with facility; data combined remote-review and AI-supported workflows.
links.quote: Bivariate results showed a strong positive association between the use of an app with tutorial videos and scan quality (OR: 14.1, 95% CI: 6.40–31.12, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Substitution of ultrasound for essential antenatal clinical assessments
links.effect: Some providers substituted ultrasound for physical examinations and vital sign checks. Findings were qualitative; resulting diagnostic errors or patient harms were not quantified.
links.quote: Although the device was widely accepted, the study revealed over-reliance on the device, with some providers substituting essential clinical practices like physical examinations and vital sign checks.

links.outcome: Provider-reported concern about loss of fundamental clinical skills
links.effect: Providers reported omitted physical examinations and concern about declining core clinical skills; actual skill decline was not objectively assessed.
links.quote: Providers noted that physical examinations were often omitted during routine check-ups, raising concerns about declining fundamental clinical skills.

links.outcome: Workflow integration and clinician workload during deployment
links.effect: Providers reported easy integration and reduced workload, but observations found overload: at least 60 pregnant women per day per facility, maximum three staff, and a healthcare provider-to-client ratio of 1:23.
links.quote: However, despite claims of reduced workload, observations revealed that healthcare providers were often overwhelmed due to high demand for ultrasounds.

links.outcome: Client experience of ultrasound-enabled antenatal care
links.effect: Clients trusted scan results but reported absent counselling and poor communication. Combined ANC assessments and scanning averaged 3–5 min versus the 30–40 min recommended standard.
links.quote: Clients expressed frustration with the lack of communication and support.

links.effect: Using an app version with tutorial videos was strongly associated with obtaining sufficient quality scans (OR 14.1).
links.quote: Bivariate results showed a strong positive association between the use of an app with tutorial videos and scan quality (OR: 14.1, 95% CI: 6.40–31.12, p < 0.001).

links.effect: Providers omitted physical examinations during routine check-ups, relying on the device instead and losing clinical skills.
links.quote: Providers noted that physical examinations were often omitted during routine check-ups, raising concerns about declining fundamental clinical skills.

links.effect: Providers incorrectly attributed the detection of vaginal odors and STIs to the ultrasound device.
links.quote: Some healthcare providers reported that the device aided in identifying additional conditions, such as Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs), by allowing them to detect vaginal odours during abdominal scans.

links.effect: High demand for ultrasounds led to overwhelming workloads and rushed examinations despite perceived efficiencies.
links.quote: However, despite claims of reduced workload, observations revealed that healthcare providers were often overwhelmed due to high demand for ultrasounds.

links.effect: Clients reported frustration due to a lack of communication and emotional support during the rapid scan encounters.
links.quote: Clients expressed frustration with the lack of communication and support.
